PLINK 2.0.0-b.1-dev (12 Oct 2026) – plink2, built without LAPACK (upstream's NOLAPACK profile: "v2.0.0-b.1-devNL")
Licence: GNU GPL 3 or later (LICENSE in this folder); its library parts also carry LGPL 3 or later notices
(LICENSE.LGPL). (C) 2005-2026 S Purcell, C Chang, B Demaille, as the program says. PLINK contains libdeflate 1.25
(MIT: LICENSE.libdeflate), zstd 1.5.7 (BSD 3-Clause or GPL 2: LICENSE.zstd, LICENSE.zstd.GPL), SIMDe 0.8.2 (MIT:
LICENSE.simde), SFMT and a part of the QD library (BSD-style: LICENSE.embedded, LICENSE.QD), and is linked with zlib 1.3.2
(LICENSE.zlib). LICENSE.embedded keeps the upstream source files that carry further notices (SFMT, fmath, the Boost
Software License parts of the statistics, QD, libdeflate's processor detection). The loader is Emscripten's runtime, with
the mailbox change of the genomics-wasm port (MIT and NCSA: LICENSE.emscripten). THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt is
genomics-wasm's summary; the "sources/" it mentions is that project's folder.
Upstream source: https://github.com/chrchang/plink-ng (commit 72119068234ce0acf7189e53dfe67a527bc53e2c, the development
version on the way to 2.0.0-b.1: not a release). The source code, as GitHub's archive of that commit (SHA-256
99cc4a517249847cfb1d3b4599dd8bc231bcd9aaff08d88e8fa569b4af060f9c; with libdeflate, zstd, SIMDe and the rest that it
bundles): ../../../licenses/sources/plink-ng-72119068234ce0acf7189e53dfe67a527bc53e2c.tar.gz. zlib 1.3.2, GitHub's
archive of its tag (SHA-256 b99a0b86c0ba9360ec7e78c4f1e43b1cbdf1e6936c8fa0f6835c0cd694a495a1):
../../../licenses/sources/zlib-1.3.2-github.tar.gz. The changes made to PLINK:
../../../licenses/genomics-wasm-build/tools/plink2/browser.patch.

Compiled to WebAssembly by the genomics-wasm project (https://github.com/comparativechrono/genomics-wasm, commit 8eea96b:
its PLINK 2 port, d68433f): Emscripten 3.1.64, with threads (pthreads in shared WebAssembly memory; the program's main
function on a thread of its own) and WebAssembly SIMD (upstream's SSE code, through SIMDe), without LAPACK. plink2.mjs
and plink2.wasm are used here as that project built them; plink2.worker.mjs, which Emscripten 3.1.64 still writes but
only as a placeholder that throws if it is loaded, is left out (the threads start from plink2.mjs itself). The page runs
each command in a worker of its own (assets/js/threads-worker.mjs), which needs a cross-origin isolated page: PLINK reads
its files on threads of their own even with --threads 1. assets/js/tools-wasm.js gives it its files – those that the
arguments name, and the files of each fileset named by a prefix (--pfile, --bfile, --pmerge-list …). Everything needed
to build it again is described in ../../../licenses/genomics-wasm-build/.

Changes to the source (browser.patch, under PLINK2_WASM_PORT only): the program does not turn on flush-to-zero for
subnormal numbers (WebAssembly has no such switch; the patched native build of the comparison does the same), and it
counts one processor unless told otherwise (a web page has no CPU affinity to ask). Statistics, file formats and
messages are PLINK's. Not in this build, which has no LAPACK: --pca and --pheno-svd (PLINK says so and stops, status 8).

In the workbench's terminal: unless they are given, the terminal adds --threads 1 --memory 640 require – as
genomics-wasm's runner does; 640 MiB is the least working memory that PLINK 2 takes – and --threads above 2 becomes 2,
--memory above 1024 becomes 1024, with a note. --script and --rerun (options read from a file) are refused: the terminal
must see those two options (and in this development version --script stops even the native program, with a buffer
overflow); plink2 $(cat FILE) does the same. --help, -h, --version and --zst-decompress are passed as they are.

Checked against PLINK 2 built natively from the same source (genomics-wasm's comparison: 41 of 41 cases, with the
unchanged native program and the native program with the port's changes – import, PGEN, VCF and BED files written by one
build and read by the other, frequencies, missingness, Hardy-Weinberg, heterozygosity, filters, LD, KING, GRM, scores,
linear, logistic and Firth regression on one and two threads, and the commands that must fail), and in the workbench,
against the unchanged native program, with the example data: every command of the help page and more (--make-bed and
--bfile, --keep, --make-king-table, --export vcf, --pmerge-list, two threads, the errors) – the same files, byte for byte,
and the same logs but for the host, the working folder, the times, the random seed and the memory found.
